messages:
Mira: heads-up — prod g4-reqpool is throwing a cluster of OOMs for redwood-alpha-7b around 23:12 UTC. not global, seems concentrated to two hosts.
Kevin: saw the alert, GPU mem climbed and KV cache retention jumped at the same time. batch sizes hit 48 -> 128 briefly.
sre-oncall: looking at traces now, KV cache miss ratio dropped then spiked, looks like prefix caching kept growing for long-context requests.
Julia: deploying a quick mitigation plan: 1) enable per-model fallthrough routing to small-variant, 2) enforce request size cap, 3) throttle large batches.
Mira: agree. can we do an emergency flag flip for fallthrough? also want to push a circuit-breaker for repeated OOMs.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.14-7 applied to config-service in 30s.
Kevin: commands to check current state:
```
# node running runtime diagnostics
curl -sS https://runtime-metrics.internal/pools/g4-reqpool/summary | jq .
ssh runtime@g4-req-12 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv'
```
Julia: circuit-breaker config snippet I'm proposing (can flip via config-service):
```
circuit_breakers:
  - id: mem_oom_fallthrough
    scope: per_host
    detection_window: 60s
    oom_threshold: 2
    cool_down: 180s
    action: route_to_variant: redwood-alpha-7b-quantized
    backoff: exponential
```
Mira: also add a request-shaping rule: cap seq_len to 4096 on hosted tier and drop heavy streaming requests into background queue with lower concurrency.
Kevin: for immediate relief I've set: `max_batch_tokens=4096` and `constrain_batching=true` on the pool. small perf hit but should stop the OOM cascade.
ops-bot: /flag set fallthrough.enabled=true for pool g4-reqpool (triggered by Kevin)
Julia: KV cache eviction tweak: lower kvcache.max_prefixs_per_model from 10000 -> 2000, and reduce ttl from 12h -> 15m for user-prefixed caches. This reduces sticky cache blowups from long chats.
Mira: good. add a telemetry checkpoint: capture a 60s heap snapshot and upload to /tmp/oom-snap-<host>.log for postmortem.
sre-oncall: capturing snapshot now, uploading. Also enabling a temporary request-level circuit to reject requests > 1e6 tokens (safety).
Kevin: post-mitigation checks: memory usage flattened, OOMs stopped after two cycles. latency increased ~8% for affected models but acceptable.
Mira: next steps to harden playbook (short list):
- permanent circuit-breaker in routing for repeated OOM patterns (per-model & per-host)
- adaptive batch-shaper: shrink batch windows when mem pressure > 75%
- buffer-reuse flag audit: we have `reuse_gpu_buffers=true` on some builds; ensure allocator safe-frees on eviction to avoid stale pointers
- automated canary: route 5% traffic to quantized variant during peak windows
- KV cache pruning: auto-evict by least-recently-used with priority for short-prefix entries
Julia: I'm creating a short runbook doc and a config patch. Will include a rollback test matrix and curl commands for emergency toggles.
Mira: nice. quick checklist for oncall to follow next time:
1) run diagnostics (curl metrics + nvidia-smi)
2) flip fallthrough flag -> route heavy requests to small variant
3) reduce max_batch_tokens + constrain batching
4) reduce kvcache limits and TTLs
5) enable per-host circuit breaker for OOM spam
6) capture heap snapshot + logs
7) escalate to runtime-eng if OOMs persist after steps 1-5
Kevin: adding a short script for toggles (quick):
```
# flip fallthrough and set batch caps
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"fallthrough":true, "max_batch_tokens":4096, "constrain_batching":true}' \
  https://config-service.internal/pools/g4-reqpool/flags
```
ops-bot: reminder — document this thread under incidents/ and attach snapshots.
Mira: thanks everyone. I'll open an incident ticket and assign postmortem to runtime-eng. leaving the short-term flags enabled for 2 hours and then we'll evaluate rollback. :thumbsup:
